sections.name: Software Engineering
sections.outcome: Change unfamiliar software systems correctly from diagnosis through implementation, migration, verification, and repository integration.
includes: Implementing specified behavior in existing or new modules
Refactoring interfaces and migrating affected code
Authoring behavioral tests and integrating build, dependency, and version-control behavior
excludes: Product requirements that do not require a code change
Pure system administration without repository changes
Algorithm exercises detached from a software system

sample_tasks.instruction: In a small library, correct one faulty conditional and add a focused regression test for the documented behavior.

In an unfamiliar multi-package project, diagnose a configuration-dependent workflow defect, add a schema-backed asynchronous API feature, refactor affected callers, update optional-dependency and version-control integration, and provide unit and end-to-end regression coverage.

sections.name: Repository Investigation and Behavioral Evidence
sections.outcome: Trace behavior through an unfamiliar repository and create tests that establish the relevant contract before and after a change.
includes: Locating public entry points and responsible implementation paths
Identifying state, control-flow, and data-flow boundaries
Constructing focused unit and integration tests with observable assertions
excludes: Choosing the final implementation of a feature or fix
Tests that only assert that code executes

sample_tasks.instruction: Locate the implementation reached by a documented public method and identify the existing test module that exercises it.

Given an unfamiliar command whose output is wrong only through its public interface, trace the call and state flow to the responsible boundary, then add a focused unit test and a command-level test that reproduce the same contract violation.

sections.name: Behavior Tracing and Fault Localization
sections.outcome: Follow an observable behavior through entry points, dispatch, state, and side effects to identify the smallest responsible code boundary.
includes: Tracing parser, callback, resolver, and command paths
Comparing expected and actual state transitions
excludes: Guessing from filenames without following execution paths
Performance profiling without a functional symptom

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace a public method call to the single helper that computes its return value.
Trace a missing command-side effect through configuration loading, dispatch, callbacks, and persistence, and identify the smallest boundary whose behavior diverges from the documented contract.

sections.name: Behavioral Test Authoring
sections.outcome: Write tests that reproduce contracts at both focused component boundaries and integrated public workflows.
includes: Regression tests that fail for the reported behavior
Assertions on values, ordering, state, emitted events, and filesystem effects
Unit and integration fixtures with controlled inputs
excludes: Tests coupled only to private implementation details
Live external-service tests when a local boundary suffices

sample_tasks.instruction: Add one assertion to an existing test that exposes the localized contract violation.

For a stateful library regression, create a focused component test for the faulty transition and a public-workflow test proving that the corrected state persists and produces the expected external effect.

sections.name: Focused Regression Tests
sections.outcome: Create small deterministic tests that isolate one semantic rule or state contract and distinguish the faulty behavior from the corrected behavior.
includes: Assertions on returned values, ordering, identity, or exceptions
Minimal fixtures that exercise one component
excludes: Assertions that merely duplicate implementation expressions

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a single failing assertion for one input at a documented boundary.
Write a compact parameterized regression suite for a range relation, covering overlap, containment, touching endpoints, reversed operand order, and disjoint inputs.

sections.name: Integrated Workflow Tests
sections.outcome: Test behavior that emerges across public APIs, callbacks, commands, files, generated artifacts, or multiple modules.
includes: Temporary filesystem, database, or schema fixtures
Assertions on cross-component state and side effects
excludes: Live network dependencies when local substitutes are available
Tests that inspect only internal call counts

sample_tasks.instruction: Run one public command in an isolated temporary workspace and assert its documented file effect.
Build an isolated workflow fixture that invokes a public command, crosses configuration and persistence boundaries, and verifies returned data, emitted output, generated files, and repository state.

sections.name: Corrective Maintenance
sections.outcome: Diagnose and repair existing behavior while preserving neighboring contracts and preventing recurrence.
includes: Parsing, detection, encoding, and resolution defects
Missing or unintended workflow side effects
excludes: Net-new product behavior without an existing contract
Suppressing failures without correcting their cause

sample_tasks.instruction: Correct an inverted boolean condition in a localized helper and extend its existing regression test.

Repair a public workflow in which encoded input is dispatched through the wrong path, mutates shared state incorrectly, and omits a configuration-gated event; preserve unaffected behavior and add focused and integrated regression tests.

sections.name: Local Contract Repair
sections.outcome: Repair localized computation, ordering, and mutable-state contracts without changing the surrounding public abstraction.
includes: Object identity and persistent mutable state

sample_tasks.instruction: Replace one incorrect comparison so a helper handles a single failing boundary case.

Repair a container whose traversal order is reversed and whose metadata accessor breaks shared identity, ensuring direct iteration, mapping views, mutation, and inherited access remain mutually consistent.

sections.name: Value, Boundary, and Ordering Semantics
sections.outcome: Correct deterministic computations whose results depend on operators, boundary conventions, evaluation modes, or traversal order.
includes: Stable forward ordering across related views

sample_tasks.instruction: Correct a helper so two ranges that only touch at an endpoint are classified according to half-open semantics.
Repair a sequence abstraction so its computation uses the documented boundary convention and its direct iteration, keys, values, and items all expose the same stable forward order.

sections.name: Identity and Mutable-State Semantics
sections.outcome: Preserve intended object identity and mutation visibility across accessors, inheritance, decorators, and repeated calls.
includes: Returning a live mutable mapping when mutation is contractual
Propagating shared state through nested contexts
excludes: Global mutable state introduced as a shortcut

sample_tasks.instruction: Change an accessor so a mutation through its returned mapping is visible on the next access.

Repair context metadata so mutations retain identity across parent and child contexts, decorator-mediated access, repeated property reads, and command execution without leaking state between independent contexts.

sections.name: Input and Resolution Pipeline Repair
sections.outcome: Repair multi-stage paths that extract structured input, select an implementation, encode identifiers, or resolve decoded data.
includes: Consistent encoding, decoding, and object lookup

sample_tasks.instruction: Correct one extraction step so an optional parsed field reaches the existing storage structure.

Repair a resource-loading path that parses a reference, detects its representation, decodes its identifier, dispatches to the proper handler, and resolves the intended object, with regression coverage at each boundary and through the public API.

sections.name: Structured Parsing Repair
sections.outcome: Correct tokenization or field extraction so structured text produces the documented normalized representation.
excludes: Selecting a parser from a file type
Adding a new grammar or serialization form

sample_tasks.instruction: Fix extraction of one optional title from an otherwise valid reference definition.

Repair reference-definition parsing so escaped labels, normalized destinations, optional titles, whitespace variants, and multiple definitions produce the correct environment entries without consuming unrelated text.

sections.name: Format Detection and Dispatch Repair
sections.outcome: Restore correct recognition and dispatch of supported inputs across validation, file inspection, and parser selection.
excludes: Implementing an entirely new file format

sample_tasks.instruction: Correct a validation branch so one documented file extension reaches its existing parser.
Repair a time-series loader so several supported binary variants pass validation, select the correct reader, and load through the public API while unsupported inputs still fail clearly.

sections.name: Encoding and Resolver Consistency
sections.outcome: Align identifier generation, decoding, type lookup, and object resolution around one round-trip contract.

sample_tasks.instruction: Make one generated identifier decode to the same type and local identifier that were supplied.
Repair a global-identifier abstraction so multiple object types and identifiers round-trip through generation and decoding and resolve correctly through an executable polymorphic query.

sections.name: Workflow Side-Effect Repair
sections.outcome: Restore intended observable effects and suppress unintended mutations in event-driven or configuration-controlled workflows.
includes: Event and log emission at the correct lifecycle point
End-to-end assertions on presence and absence of effects
excludes: Changing message wording without behavioral impact
Manual repository cleanup instead of fixing the workflow

sample_tasks.instruction: Restore one missing informational event at the existing successful-completion hook.

Repair a configurable pipeline so successful responses emit their expected lifecycle events while generated files are staged only when automatic staging is enabled, covering enabled and disabled modes end to end.

sections.name: Lifecycle Event Restoration
sections.outcome: Reconnect missing logs, signals, or callbacks to the correct processing stage without duplicating or reordering work.
includes: Finding the lifecycle hook that owns an event
Preserving status, method, and resource context
Testing event level, multiplicity, and ordering
excludes: Changing core processing solely to produce a log

sample_tasks.instruction: Emit one missing success log from the existing response-completion hook.
Restore response lifecycle reporting so redirects, successes, and failures emit exactly the expected contextual events in processing order without changing request handling.

sections.name: Configuration-Gated Mutation Repair
sections.outcome: Ensure commands mutate files, indexes, or external state only when the controlling configuration authorizes that mutation.
includes: Separating file generation from repository staging

sample_tasks.instruction: Guard one existing staging call with the already-defined automatic-staging setting.

Repair a reproduction command so generated manifests, locks, and metrics remain unstaged by default and are staged consistently when automatic staging is enabled, including repeated and partially tracked runs.

sections.name: Feature Engineering from Specification
sections.outcome: Translate a behavioral specification into a coherent public API and implementation spanning the necessary components.
excludes: Repairs that only restore an existing contract

sample_tasks.instruction: Add one optional public argument, forward it to an existing implementation branch, and test its observable effect.

Add a declarative job feature whose public API accepts heterogeneous operations, whose schema selects serialized forms, whose asynchronous coordinator manages ownership, and whose implementation is separated into reusable modules with end-to-end tests.

sections.name: Public API Extension
sections.outcome: Extend an established API with new options or flexible operations while preserving existing conventions and behavior.
includes: Validation and normalization of heterogeneous requests
Named outputs and documented return shapes

sample_tasks.instruction: Add one optional formatting argument with a constant value and apply it at the existing rendering boundary.
Extend a tabular API with named and positional aggregation specifications while also supporting a callable output modifier, normalizing both forms consistently and preserving existing calls.

sections.name: Narrow Option and Attribute Extensions
sections.outcome: Add a bounded parameter or declarative attribute and propagate it through parsing, precedence, implementation, and output.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a constant string option to one public method and apply it to each emitted line.

Add a field-level generated-type override that is parsed from an attribute, takes documented precedence over inferred optionality, appears in generated output, and leaves fields without the attribute unchanged.

sections.name: Heterogeneous Operation APIs
sections.outcome: Design and implement an API that normalizes multiple selection and operation forms into deterministic grouped results.
includes: String operations, callables, and named outputs

sample_tasks.instruction: Allow one named aggregation over one explicitly selected column in an existing grouped operation.
Implement grouped summarization supporting individual columns, column lists, pattern selectors, named aggregations, string operations, and callables with deterministic output naming and shape.

sections.name: Schema-Driven Serialization Features
sections.outcome: Extend a schema and its generated artifacts so field metadata selects and executes the correct structured serialization behavior.
includes: Routing values to text or JSON message parsers
excludes: Fixing dispatch for an already-supported file format
Ad hoc parsing that bypasses schema metadata

sample_tasks.instruction: Add one schema enum value and expose it through the generated field metadata.

Add field-level selection between default, text, and JSON representations for nested messages, regenerate bindings, propagate metadata through configuration loading, and parse each form through the proper serializer.

sections.name: Asynchronous Coordination Protocols
sections.outcome: Implement reusable asynchronous ownership coordination with correct acquisition, renewal, loss, release, cancellation, and callback semantics.
includes: Timed state transitions and retry behavior
excludes: Synchronous blocking inside the event loop
Consensus algorithms beyond the specified lease protocol

sample_tasks.instruction: Adapt one blocking lock-acquisition operation into a cancellable asynchronous method while preserving its result contract.

Implement a reusable asynchronous leader-election component that acquires and renews a lease, handles contention and lease loss, invokes start and stop callbacks once, relinquishes ownership on cancellation, and supports deterministic behavioral tests.

sections.name: Multi-Module System Synthesis
sections.outcome: Implement a cohesive small system whose modules have explicit dependency direction, testable public interfaces, and coordinated stateful and filesystem behavior.
includes: Separating foundational operations, data processing, and orchestration
Deterministic traversal, aggregation, and permission effects
excludes: Placing all logic in one script
External dependencies when the specification forbids them
Duplicating lower-layer logic in orchestration code

sample_tasks.instruction: Create a foundational module and one dependent module that imports a single public helper and exposes a tested wrapper.

Build a standard-library project with a transactional migration layer, a deterministic depth-bounded file-analysis layer, and an orchestration layer that applies permissions and produces reports through explicit one-way imports.

sections.name: Refactoring and Code Migration
sections.outcome: Change software structure or interfaces while preserving behavior and migrating every affected consumer and artifact.
includes: Changing public signatures with coordinated caller updates
Migrating schemas, generated code, documentation, and tests
excludes: Behavioral feature work unrelated to the migration

sample_tasks.instruction: Rename a private helper and update its direct callers and tests without changing behavior.

Extract a public subsystem into a new module boundary, revise its interface, migrate internal and external callers, update schema-derived artifacts and packaging exports, and prove behavioral equivalence with focused and integrated tests.

sections.name: Structure-Preserving Refactoring
sections.outcome: Improve module, function, or dependency structure while preserving externally observable behavior.
includes: Maintaining dependency direction and public exports
excludes: Retaining dead paths for speculative compatibility

sample_tasks.instruction: Extract one repeated computation into a shared function and update both callers.
Separate a mixed filesystem workflow into computation, persistence, and orchestration modules, remove duplicate implementations, preserve public results and side effects, and keep imports acyclic.

sections.name: Cross-Layer Interface Migration
sections.outcome: Migrate an interface change consistently through declarations, implementations, generated artifacts, callers, tests, documentation, and exports.
includes: Updating all call sites and generated bindings
excludes: Backward-compatibility aliases without an explicit requirement

sample_tasks.instruction: Change one function parameter name and update every in-repository caller and test.

Replace a public configuration field with a typed representation and migrate its schema, generated bindings, parser, runtime consumers, exports, examples, and regression tests without retaining the old path.

sections.name: Repository, Dependency, and Version-Control Integration
sections.outcome: Integrate code changes with optional dependencies, packaging, generated artifacts, and version-control workflows without producing unintended repository state.
includes: Runtime availability checks and annotation-safe imports
excludes: Installing tools only in a local shell
General Git usage unrelated to application behavior

sample_tasks.instruction: Move one optional-library reference so importing the package succeeds when that library is absent.

Integrate an optional plugin whose annotated API remains importable without its dependency, whose extra is packaged correctly, and whose generation command updates files while staging them only under the repository's automatic-staging setting.

sections.name: Optional Dependency and Packaging Boundaries
sections.outcome: Keep packages importable and accurately feature-gated when optional libraries are present or absent.
includes: Separating type annotations from runtime availability checks
Lazy or guarded optional imports at established boundaries
Testing installed and missing dependency states
excludes: Broad exception handling around arbitrary imports

sample_tasks.instruction: Prevent one type annotation from forcing import of an optional plotting library.
Repair an optional visualization feature so package import, capability detection, annotated public APIs, and failure messages behave correctly both with and without the plotting extra installed.

sections.name: Version-Control-Aware Command Behavior
sections.outcome: Make repository commands create, modify, and stage artifacts exactly as their version-control configuration specifies.
includes: Testing tracked, untracked, enabled, and disabled cases
excludes: Hard-coded Git commands that bypass project abstractions
Deleting user changes to obtain a clean state

sample_tasks.instruction: Make one generated file remain unstaged when automatic staging is disabled.

Implement command behavior that updates manifests, locks, and metrics while preserving unrelated index entries and staging generated artifacts only when automatic staging is enabled across new, modified, and repeated runs.
